mcfinley October 2, 2025, 2:31pm 3

Structured outputs is the way to go if you have complex records and rigid requirements for outputs. The tech under the hood for it is not just a fine tune… OpenAI actually ensures the production of each token follows the pattern you define inside the transformer itself, so your output structure is guided during the generation process, not as an output filter.

Another option is to make your output record definition look like a tool call… the model thinks its calling a tool but you use the tool parameter list as a structured output instead. Gets you some of the benefits and arguably more flexibility since you can still get other modalities of output tokens.

If you want to stick to the approach you have now, just ask the model to generate json, here are some of my best practices:

  * use the chat API and treat each request like a multi-turn conversation with built-in checks that iterates until the json is valid. Put your record format in the system/developer prompt, then your initial request in the first user prompt. 
I only use regex to parse streaming json that lets me tell the user what’s going on before the model is done. For long records, I don’t want to wait without giving the user feedback so I need to be able to recognize what the model is streaming and tell the user something like “One moment, field 5 ot 12 is complete…”

that last approach ends up looking like

system: please make an array of recods in json for any dates mentioned in the following text. each record should have the fields “year” and “month” as strings. mark the start of your json with JSON: and end with a new line. today is October 2, 2025.
